catalog.eyebrow: A catalogue with no index server
catalog.title: Kouigenji Monogatari — volume catalogue
catalog.lead: TEI/XML of the Genji Monogatari variorum (Ikeda Kikan, Chuokoron-sha), published volume by volume. The text is CC0; no permission is needed to read it. Each volume carries a proof that it belongs to the anchored set of 54, checkable without looking at the other volumes. This page is assembled directly from the chain, with no Ocean node and no index server.
catalog.footnote: Each root is anchored in CorpusAnchor ({anchor}). The text lives on IPFS and can be fetched by anyone from a public gateway. Reference counts are read from on-chain order records, which the publisher cannot alter.

lineage.title: Where this interface comes from
lineage.note: Ocean Market, the Pontus-X Portal and Clio-X are all descendants of the same interface, sharing the card layout (the git history carries 1,155 commits by Ocean's own developers). The composition here is borrowed too, with one change: where they show a price, this shows how many times the item has been referenced. Keeping a price slot when nothing is for sale would be a lie, and what this system counts is use, not ownership. One more difference: they read from an index server (Aquarius); this reads straight from the chain.

search.placeholder: Filter by title or number (e.g. kiritsubo, 05)
search.wakaNote: This one is counted from the TEI, not recorded on chain.

catalog.readAt: Read from the chain at block {block}

whole.title: All 54 volumes as a single record
whole.body: Alongside the 54 per-volume records, the same text is published as one TEI/XML file. {lines} lines. It carries no per-volume inclusion proof; those live on the individual volumes.

read.title: Read the text
read.lead: It is CC0. No permission is needed — the link below works right now. It is stored content-addressed (CID), so the same address resolves no matter who serves it.
read.xmlNote: This is a raw TEI/XML file. Your browser may show a blank page or a parse error — it is namespaced XML and the browser has no way to render it. The bytes do arrive; they just cannot be displayed. You can see the content under "Check it yourself" below.

get.title: Record that you consulted this version
get.note: Pressing this does not give you the text — you can already read it above. What it gives you is evidence: a permanent public record that you consulted this exact version. Put the receipt in a footnote and, five years later, it stays clear which version you read. Free, but it costs gas (Sepolia test ETH).
get.howTo: How to get gas, step by step →

verify.title: Check it yourself
verify.lead: You do not have to trust this page. Press the button and your own browser fetches the text from a public IPFS gateway, hashes it, and folds {proof} hashes ({bytes} bytes) up to the root of all {total} volumes. It never touches the other volumes.

step.fetch: Fetch the text from a public gateway
step.hash: Hash it and compare with the claim
step.fold: Fold the proof path up to the root

verify.ok: Verified. This text is part of the root anchored on chain.
verify.note: This runs entirely in your browser. It does not go through this site's server, an Ocean node, or an index server.
verify.preview: Show the beginning of the fetched text
verify.previewNote: These are the exact bytes just used for verification. No extra request was made.

raw.title: Raw values
raw.ddoValue: {n} bytes, stored unencrypted on chain, so readers need no server
raw.author: Author

ddo.help: From the DDO recorded on chain. This is what the publisher asserted; the chain does not vouch for it.

chain.help: Held by the chain itself, read from a contract or an event. The publisher cannot alter it after the fact.

tei.help: Counted from the TEI here. Not recorded on chain. Anyone with the text can recompute it.

text.title: About the text
text.note: Only this group can be checked from outside. Given the text, anyone can recompute these values and compare.

catalogue.title: Catalogue record
catalogue.note: Written to fit the Ocean format. How the DID is derived and how the data NFT is shaped are both Ocean decisions.

usage.title: Reference records
usage.note: Who consulted this, and when, accumulates on this datatoken. It is free, so anyone can add as many as they like. The count itself proves nothing.

asset.caveat: Only the publisher has anchored this. It becomes a record the publisher cannot erase only once independent third parties anchor the same root. Also, being on IPFS does not mean permanent: if nobody keeps it, it becomes unreachable.

count.title: Times referenced
count.caveat: Anyone can add one for free. A high count is not evidence that the material is well used.

txs.title: Transactions for this volume
txs.note: Only the ones this catalogue tracks. Each is annotated, showing which transaction put the values on chain.

contract.factsNote: name and symbol are what the contract itself claims. The chain guarantees only that the code at this address answered this way — not that the claim is true. Anyone can deploy a contract with the same name.
contract.rawNote: Beyond this point the interface is generic, and some of what it shows is hard to read in this context (the things explained above actually appear there).

dataNft.title: A catalogue entry (data NFT)
dataNft.what: This is not the material itself. It represents the role of publishing this material. Whoever holds it can rewrite the metadata and issue datatokens. Hand it to a library and the role moves; the text does not (the text lives on IPFS and anyone can read it).
dataNft.gotcha: Etherscan shows "1 of ...". That 1 is an ID, not a quantity. Each ERC-721 token has its own number, so you ask ownerOf(1) for its holder. Issuance is recorded as a transfer "from address zero" — there is no dedicated mint display.

datatoken.title: A use token (datatoken)
datatoken.what: A ticket for one use of the material. Nobody ever holds one: ordering mints a token, records the order, and burns it inside the same transaction. What remains is only the record that it was used.
datatoken.gotcha: The Holders tab on Etherscan looks empty. Nothing is broken — the supply is always zero. There is no tradeable holding; what is counted is use, not ownership.

corpusAnchor.title: Where roots are anchored (CorpusAnchor)
corpusAnchor.what: A contract for recording the roots that fold all 54 volumes, and all 25,065 lines, into a single value each. Anyone can call it. If another researcher or library runs the same computation and gets the same root, they can anchor it under their own name.
corpusAnchor.gotcha: This contract holds no state variables at all, so there is no way to ask "what is the latest root?" — you read the whole log instead. That is deliberate: a single writable variable would be enough for the publisher to erase the past. Here, overwriting simply does not exist as an operation.

factory.title: The factory (ERC721Factory)
factory.what: Ocean deployed this on Sepolia. One call to it creates a catalogue entry and a datatoken at once. Everyone uses this same factory.

dispenser.title: The dispenser
dispenser.what: The counter that hands out tokens for free assets. It is a single shared contract, not one created per asset.
dispenser.gotcha: Publishing emits an event called DispenserCreated, but nothing was created. This asset’s distribution settings were merely registered with the shared counter. The name is misleading.

nftTemplate.title: The catalogue entry implementation (ERC721Template)
nftTemplate.what: The actual behaviour of every catalogue entry lives here. Each entry is a 45-byte shell that forwards everything to this address. Deploying the full implementation each time would cost millions of gas.

dtTemplate.title: The use token implementation (ERC20Template)
dtTemplate.what: The behaviour of every datatoken lives here. Each datatoken is itself a 45-byte proxy. Ocean Market defaults to this "Enterprise" version, which mints, records and burns in one transaction.

feeCollector.title: The fee recipient (OPFCommunityFeeCollector)
feeCollector.what: Where Ocean community fees go. This material is free, so nothing has ever flowed here.

row.name: Claimed name
row.codeProxyNote: Only 45 bytes, because this is a minimal proxy. It forwards every call to the implementation below and does nothing else. That is why Etherscan shows no source on the Contract tab.
row.proxyTargetNote: The program at this address runs. It is shared by everyone.
row.ownerNote: The answer to ownerOf(1). This account can rewrite the metadata.
row.supply721Note: Just one. ERC-721 tokens are each distinct, so this count and the ID are different things.
row.supply20Note: Always zero: minted and burned inside the same transaction as the order.
row.capNote: Not honoured by every datatoken implementation. It is honoured by Ocean Market's default (Enterprise).
row.pairedNoteDt: The catalogue entry that issues this token.

contract.txsNote: Only the ones this catalogue tracks: transactions addressed to it, and transactions in which it emitted a record.

order.title: Reference record
order.what: This transaction left a record that someone consulted this volume. One datatoken was minted, handed to the caller, and burned within the same transaction. What remains is not the datatoken but the record of the reference.
order.gotcha: A reference record says nothing about whether the text is intact. Anyone can trigger one for free, so a high count means nothing. Whether the text was altered is settled by the root instead.

anchor.title: Root record
anchor.what: This transaction recorded a root for the whole corpus. With that root, any one of the 25,065 lines can be shown to have been part of that version using 15 hashes. The 5.87 MB of text never has to change hands.
anchor.gotcha: Roots are appended, never overwritten. Each time the source is corrected a new root is recorded, and the older ones stay. Which one is current is decided by whoever reads the records in order.

metadata.title: Metadata record
metadata.what: This transaction wrote the volume metadata (DDO) onto the chain. It is not encrypted, so reading it needs no server.
metadata.gotcha: In August 2026 all 55 records were rewritten to take the publisher name out of the metadata. The earlier versions carrying the name remain on the chain. They cannot be removed.

tx.logsNote: The {n} records in the order the chain wrote them. The number on the left is the index within the block, the same number Etherscan shows.

transfer.mint: One datatoken was newly minted. A sender of the zero address is the marker for "newly created".
transfer.move: That same one moved to its next holder.
transfer.burn: The datatoken was burned. A recipient of the zero address is the marker for "gone". It was held only for a few log entries inside this same transaction.

note.TokensDispensed: The Dispenser recorded that it handed one out. The Dispenser is a shared Ocean contract, not something built for this material.
note.OrderStarted: This is the line that matters. The record that this version was consulted is left in a form nobody can erase. The other entries are the procedure that leaves this one line.
note.ProviderFee: Every provider fee field is zero. Ocean normally verifies a provider signature before an order goes through, but with the fee address set to zero, the address recovered from an empty signature is also zero, so the two match. That is why no Ocean node has to run at all.
note.CorpusAnchored: One root was recorded. The contract is open to anyone on purpose. Only when someone else records the same root can it be said that the publisher did not reconstruct it afterwards.
note.unknown: No note prepared for this record yet. See Etherscan for the raw values.
note.MetadataCreated: The metadata for this volume was written to the chain for the first time.
note.MetadataUpdated: The metadata was rewritten. The earlier version remains; nothing can be removed from the chain.

tx.factsNote: None of these are claims. They are values the chain itself holds.
tx.actorsNote: Addresses this catalogue can explain link inward. The rest link out to Etherscan.
tx.rawNote: The unannotated screen is here, to read alongside the notes above.

row.treeSizeNote: Verification needs this number because it fixes the shape of the tree. 54 is the per-volume tree, 25,065 the per-line tree.
row.specNote: How leaves are formed and how the tree is built. A root whose method is unknown cannot be checked, so the two are recorded together.
row.sourceUriNote: Which state of the text it was computed from. It points at a git commit.
row.fromNote: Who paid the gas. This can differ from the consumer named in the record — anyone can name someone else as the consumer.
row.toNote: The contract this transaction spoke to.
row.selectorNote: Derived from the first four bytes of the call data. Etherscan sometimes leaves it as hex.
row.valueNote: Zero. A datatoken has no price.
row.feeNote: Goes to the validator that built the block. It is not payment for the datatoken.
row.changeNote: Rewriting does not remove the previous version. Nothing can be deleted from the chain.
row.flagsPlainNote: 0x00 marks it as not encrypted, which is why reading it needs no server.
row.flagsNote: Anything other than 0x00 means encryption or compression, which needs separate machinery to read.

footer.bottom: TEI data is CC0 1.0. The interface is ported from Ocean Market / Pontus-X Portal / Clio-X (Apache-2.0). Assembled directly from the chain and IPFS, with no index server.

wallet.disconnectNote: Also revokes the permission in your wallet. If your wallet does not support that, only this page disconnects.

prefs.appearanceHelp: Defaults to your OS setting, select to override.

hero.title: Kouigenji Monogatari Text DB — web3 edition
hero.lead: The same text database, assembled directly from a chain and IPFS. The text stays CC0 and needs no permission to read. What this edition adds is three things: (1) each volume carries a proof that it belongs to the anchored whole, checkable without touching the other volumes; (2) you can leave a citation that nobody can erase; (3) the catalogue needs no index server, so it keeps working if the operator stops.
hero.upstream: The original site (full-text search, SPARQL and IIIF are better there)

read.title: To read
read.body: The text lives on IPFS and anyone can fetch it from a public gateway. No login, no token. It is CC0, so use it freely.

cite.title: To cite
cite.body: You can leave an on-chain record that you consulted this version. Put the transaction hash in a footnote and it stays clear five years later which version you read.

verify.title: To check
verify.body: You do not have to trust what this page says. Your own browser fetches the text, hashes it, and walks a 192-byte proof path up to the root.

behind.title: What is behind this page
behind.body: Ocean Market, the Pontus-X Portal and Clio-X are all descendants of the same interface, and so is this page (its CSS and components are ported from them). One thing differs: they read from an index server (Aquarius); this reads straight from the chain and IPFS. The reason is concrete — Ocean's index server went down and Ocean Market showed zero items.
behind.readAt: Read from the chain at block {block} / CorpusAnchor {anchor}

whole.link: See all 54 volumes as a single record

upstream.title: How this relates to the upstream site
upstream.body: This is not a replacement for the upstream site. Full-text search, SPARQL, IIIF and rendering speed are all better there. Four things are added here: a fixed version, a record of citation, third-party verification, and per-volume reference counts.

about.title: About this prototype
about.lead: A prototype that publishes the Kouigenji Monogatari TEI/XML without an index server.

caveat.title: Caveats
caveat.body: This is a prototype, running on a test network. The root was anchored by the publisher alone, so at this stage it is no more than a record the publisher wrote about themselves. It starts to mean something only once an independent third party runs the same computation and anchors the same root. And putting the text on IPFS does not make it permanent: if nobody keeps holding it, it stops being retrievable.

missing.title: What is not here
missing.body: Some features of the upstream portal were left out. There is nothing behind them here, so porting them would only produce empty panels.
missing.item1: Publishing and editing (there is a single publisher, and nothing is published through the interface)
missing.item2: Buying and pricing (the text is CC0, so there is nothing to sell)
missing.item3: Compute-to-Data (there is no compute environment to run jobs in)

what.title: What this does
what.body: The Kouigenji Monogatari text database (TEI/XML based on Ikeda Kikan, Chuokoron-sha) is published as 55 entries: the 54 volumes plus the whole. The catalogue is read straight from on-chain metadata, and the text itself comes from IPFS. There is no database and no index server behind this page.

data.title: Source text and licence
data.body: The base text is Ikeda Kikan's Kouigenji Monogatari (Chuokoron-sha). The TEI/XML is published on the upstream site under CC0 1.0. No permission or account is needed to read it.

chain.title: What lives on chain
chain.body: Three kinds of contract sit on Sepolia, an Ethereum test network: a data NFT that stands for the role of publishing a volume, a datatoken that covers a single access, and CorpusAnchor, which records the root that folds all 54 volumes into one value. Each contract has its own page explaining what Etherscan is actually showing you.

lineage.title: Where the interface comes from
lineage.body: The interface is ported from Ocean Market (Ocean Protocol) by way of deltaDAO's Pontus-X Portal and Clio-X, under Apache-2.0. The CSS and the DOM structure are carried over as they are, rather than reimplemented from the look of them. Only two things changed: routing (Pages Router to App Router) and where the data comes from (the chain and IPFS directly, instead of the Aquarius index server).

whole.title: All 54 volumes as a single record
whole.body: Alongside the 54 per-volume records, the same text is published as one TEI/XML file of 25,065 lines. It is a different level of granularity, so it is kept out of the per-volume listing.

upstream.title: What the upstream site does better
upstream.body: This is not a replacement for the upstream site (the Kouigenji Monogatari text database). Full-text search, the SPARQL endpoint, IIIF alignment with page images, and plain rendering speed are all better there. Only four things are added here.
upstream.item1: A fixed version. Which state of the text a citation points at can no longer be moved after the fact.
upstream.item2: A record of citation. Consulting the text can be recorded on chain, so a footnote can carry the transaction hash.
upstream.item3: Third-party verification. You do not have to trust this page; your own browser can recompute the root.
upstream.item4: Per-volume reference counts. The record of who consulted what, and when, lives outside the publisher's hands.

publisher.title: The key behind these records
publisher.lead: All 55 entries in this catalogue were recorded from a single key. What is written on chain is only that key’s address — no name appears anywhere. This page bridges the address to a person.

onChain.title: What the chain guarantees
onChain.note: Everything below can be read back from Sepolia by anyone. The publisher cannot alter it after the fact.
onChain.author: DDO author field
onChain.authorNote: In all {n} records this field holds the address itself. No name is present.
onChain.anchorNote: The root of the 54 volumes and the root of all 25,065 lines are recorded in this contract.

offChain.title: From here on, this is only a claim
offChain.warn: None of this section is on chain. This page is simply asserting it, and it can be deleted. Delete it and the address above becomes just an address again. It is arranged this way so that personal data is never placed somewhere it cannot be withdrawn (EDPB guidelines on blockchain, 02/2025).
offChain.name: Claimed by
offChain.signatureNote: The statement below, signed with the key for the address above ({scheme}). Nobody else could produce it.

verify.title: Check it yourself
verify.note: You do not have to take our word for it. With foundry’s cast and jq you can verify the signature.
verify.expect: If it prints Validation succeeded and shows {address}, the claim holds.

creators.title: The people who made the data are different
creators.body: This key only put the records on chain. The Kouigenji Monogatari TEI/XML itself is the work of several people; the list of contributors is on the original site and in the TEI header. Their names appear neither on chain nor on this page, because consent was not obtained.

howTo.title: How to record a citation
howTo.lead: You need nothing at all to read. The text is CC0, lives on IPFS, and opens from a link. Setup is only needed to write "I cited this version" onto the chain, and for that you need one thing: gas on a test network.

terms.title: Three words first
terms.note: People read this as "you need a token". That is not quite right.

eth.name: ETH
eth.body: The base currency of Ethereum. It is not a token. Tokens are issued by a contract; ETH has no contract — the chain itself tracks balances. Here you use ETH on Sepolia, a test network, which cannot be exchanged for money.

datatoken.name: datatoken
datatoken.body: The token Ocean Protocol uses. You do not supply it. Pressing "Record" mints exactly one inside that transaction and burns it in the same one. So nobody can hold it and nobody can trade it. Supply is always zero.

gas.name: Gas
gas.body: The fee for having the network execute a write. Paid in ETH by whoever writes. Reading costs nothing.

wallet.title: Install a wallet
wallet.body: A browser extension such as MetaMask. If you already have one, use it.

network.title: Switch to Sepolia
network.body: This catalogue uses only Sepolia, a test network. Nothing is on a production chain. If the top right does not say Sepolia, press the wallet button and it will ask to switch.

faucet.title: Get some test ETH
faucet.body: Sepolia ETH comes free from a faucet. It cannot be exchanged for money, so no real value moves. One record costs very little — 0.01 ETH covers dozens. Any of these will do.

order.title: Press "Record" on a volume page
order.body: Your wallet asks you to sign. Approving leaves an on-chain record that you cited this version. It does not deliver the text (you can already read it). What you get is a citation nobody can erase.

noEth.q: It says I do not have enough gas
noEth.a: The faucet ETH has not arrived yet, or it arrived on a different network. Check that your wallet shows Sepolia and that the balance is not zero.

wrongChain.q: It says to switch to Sepolia
wrongChain.a: You are on a production network. Press the button at the top right and it will ask to switch. If declined, choose Sepolia manually in your wallet.

noWallet.a: The extension is not installed, or is disabled for this tab. Reload the page after installing.

nothing.q: Do I need to record anything at all?
nothing.a: No. Not for reading. It matters when you want a footnote that pins down which version you saw, so that later updates cannot blur it.

howTo.readOnly: To repeat: reading needs no setup. Open the text straight from the catalogue.
